questions.questionText: Explain how hashing works under the hood in a Hash Map, and how hash collisions are typically resolved in standard libraries.
questions.studentAnswer: Stack memory is used for static allocation and thread execution frames with O(1) push and pop. Heap memory is allocated dynamically for objects and survives beyond the function scope, managed by garbage collection.

evaluation.instantFeedback: Good foundational response. You covered the core definition of Data Structures & Algorithms, but can stand out further by discussing edge cases, memory/computational complexity, or production failure modes.
strengths: Identified the correct purpose and standard implementation of Data Structures & Algorithms
Adequate clarity and understandable communication flow
areasToImprove: Include deeper architectural trade-offs (e.g. memory vs speed)
Reference a concrete production scenario or practical bug you resolved
evaluation.idealAnswerSummary: A comprehensive answer for "Data Structures & Algorithms" covers: 1) Underlying architecture and data flow, 2) Performance implications (Big-O / latency), 3) Comparison of trade-offs against alternative approaches, and 4) Practical hands-on examples.
